findings: Accepts supplied item/discharge records; does not load the graph or execute evidence. Source descriptors and evidence strings are descriptive.
Explicit discharges use exact premise/scope ID pairs; item propagation requires an explicit export scope and literal effective status DISCHARGED. VERIFIED alone does not propagate.
Absent explicit frontier_state, arbitrary nonempty statuses outside the open heuristic become CLOSED in item_observations. FAILED reproduces this default; explicit OPEN avoids it.

history.input_fingerprint binds normalized historical items only. Different discharge overlays can produce different open sets with identical history fingerprints; this is not a complete current-observation identity.
Historical records are deep-normalized and projection copies preserve input objects. Stored immutable flags do not prevent later caller mutation of returned dictionaries.
does_not_discharge is descriptive and not used as a separate constraint. No geometric containment or scope weakening is inferred.
The fixed-point loop has a len(items)+1 bound and refuses nonconvergence. General status transition/cycle semantics are not proven; do not adopt this as the proposed kernel.
proposed_repairs: Require explicit OPEN/CLOSED state or a typed exhaustive status mapping when producing shared observations; unknown statuses should not silently close work.
Expose distinct historical-input and complete-observation fingerprints where consumers require both.
Keep supplied discharge assertions separate from admitted warrants; require replay/binding at any future authority boundary.
remaining: Adversarial cycle/status-transition controls and consumer fingerprint use need further semantic review.
Neutral source/history extraction remains incomplete; no gate completion claimed.
